desc: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) isn’t just an adult issue, it happens in kids too.  These are the kiddos who have belly pain in the morning, spend hours on the toilet, have constipation or diarrhea (often a mix of both) and pain resolves after pooping.  It’s a diagnosis of exclusion, meaning there’s no test but it’s important to be evaluated by a Pediatric Gastroenterologist  to make sure these symptoms dont represent signs of another condition.  If you think your child has IBS feel free to DM me

desc:
You know the cramp 😭 The one where you’re suddenly hunched over because standing up straight is NOT an option.

That intense “poop cramp” is usually caused by strong contractions of the intestines as your gut works to move stool and gas through. When the bowel stretches from stool or trapped gas, it can trigger visceral pain and spasms that feel sharp, deep, and sometimes bad enough to make you instinctively curl forward.

Basically: your intestines are squeezing, your pain receptors are yelling
